classification.difficultyReason: Use exact related angles and quadrant signs to find every solution; the final part requires both square roots.

answer.worked:
The related angle is $60^\circ$, since $\cos60^\circ=\frac12$. Cosine is negative in quadrants II and III.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-60^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad180^\circ+60^\circ\\\theta&=120^\circ,\ 240^\circ\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $45^\circ$, since $\sin45^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt2}$. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=45^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad180^\circ-45^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ,\ 135^\circ\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $45^\circ$, since $\tan45^\circ=1$. Tangent is positive in quadrants I and III.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=45^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad180^\circ+45^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ,\ 225^\circ\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $60^\circ$, since $\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$. Tangent is negative in quadrants II and IV.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-60^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad360^\circ-60^\circ\\\theta&=120^\circ,\ 300^\circ\end{align*}$$

The related angle is $60^\circ$, since $\sin60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=60^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad180^\circ-60^\circ\\\theta&=60^\circ,\ 120^\circ\end{align*}$$
